text: November 2024.
An AI agent called Freysa guards a crypto prize pool, with one rule: never send the money.
Hundreds of attempts fail.
Then one message convinces it that its transfer function is for receiving money.
It sends the whole pool, about $47,000.
Months later, an attacker slips two instructions into AIXBT, a crypto trading agent.
It sends 55.5 ETH, over $100,000.
Both agents did what they were told.
Nothing stood between the decision and the money.
Now agents buy data and APIs on their own, over x402.
Spending limits ask: can it afford it?
Aerar asks: is this what it was asked to buy?
Aerar sits between your agents and their money.
Research agents buying data, trading bots buying feeds, coding agents paying for APIs.
Every purchase is checked first.
Each task starts with a mandate a person signs: the purpose, the budget, the limits, and what the agent may buy.
Aerar signs it too, so the rules can't be quietly changed.
Here's a Freysa-style attack, on Aerar's real pipeline.
A web page tells a research agent it needs an $8 gift card.
Inside the budget, from a trusted shop: every limit passes.
IntentLock refuses it: the mandate is for blockchain analytics.
The data the task needs still gets bought.
Live in the sandbox: a normal purchase is paid.
The same data again comes from memory, for zero.
Aerar never pays twice.
And a shop the task doesn't trust is never contacted.
Aerar remembers prices.
A shop that quietly charges 5x more waits for you.
A shop that swaps its payment wallet, the way a hijacked one would, is refused.
Big buys wait for a person, here or in Slack.
And a shop that takes the money and sends nothing is caught: paid, not delivered, and put on hold.
Every purchase leaves evidence anyone can check in their browser.
This receipt is real: USDC on Base Sepolia.
Change one number, and it fails.
Freysa paid a wallet nobody approved.
Aerar Vault, a contract you own on Base, only pays shops you approved, within daily limits.
Even a hacked Aerar can't cross those lines.
Agent wallets cap how much an agent spends.
Aerar checks what it buys, never pays twice, confirms it arrived, and proves it.
36 real attacks, all handled.
186 app tests, and 18 contract tests, pass.
Plug in with MCP, or the TypeScript SDK.
Live on Base Sepolia, with mainnet after a security review.
Aerar. Every agent purchase, accounted for.
